title: M.A. in Hindi / a Regional Language

value.body: A two-year Master's in Hindi or another Indian language. It goes deeper into literary history, criticism, linguistics and, in many universities, translation studies and functional writing. It is also the usual qualification for translator, Rajbhasha and college-teaching posts in the language.

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A bachelor's degree, usually with the language as a subject. Central universities admit through CUET-PG; state universities use their own entrance tests or graduation marks.

value.title: At a glance
items: Large distance and open-university enrolment exists alongside regular programmes.
Common next steps are UGC-NET, a Ph.D., a B.Ed, or translator and Rajbhasha exams.
Private-sector work is mostly in media, publishing, translation and content.
